content.content:
#### Image

Runs use an image the application builds itself, with `podman build`, and keeps up to date: the default image, holding the harness commands, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, and piton, each at the version installed on the host where it can be found there, and at its latest otherwise. It is built again when any of those versions changes.
Each command the image holds has to run in it, not only be there. The build ends by running each one's version command in the image, as `piton --version`, and a build where one fails, as a piton built against a newer C library than the image has, fails, saying which command couldn't run and what it printed. An image whose piton can't run is never used, so a Spec run is never sent where it can't run `piton build` to check its work.
A project can add to it with a Containerfile of its own, `.suspense/Containerfile`, built FROM the default image, to add what its runs in a container need, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says. The project's image is built from it, and kept, and built again only when the Containerfile or the default image changes. Without one, the project's runs use the default image.
While an image is being built for a run, the task or question shows "Preparing environment" as its status, and what the build prints goes to its raw output. A build that fails fails the run, saying why.
The image is a Linux image, whatever the host is, so what it holds is installed in it for Linux, for the architecture Podman runs: each harness and piton at the version found on the host, from its own Linux release or package, never a binary copied from the host, which on macOS or Windows can't run in it. The build is given only the Containerfile the application writes for it, in a build context of its own, a fresh temporary directory holding nothing else, never the project or the user's home, and needs nothing from the host but the network.
Each harness is installed in a step of its own, so one that can't be installed never stops the others. A version taken from the host is used only once the package registry is asked, before the build, and has it, as `npm view <package>@<version> version` answering it; the version a host's command prints is read only as a plain version number, never with anything printed around it. A version the registry doesn't have, one that can't be read, or one not published for Linux, is installed at its latest instead, never failing the build, and the welcome page and the Settings' Containers section say which harness runs a different version in its container than on the host, muted, never as an error. A harness that can't be installed at all is left out of the image, which still builds, and only runs that need it fail, as below.
Only one build of an image runs at a time. A run, a login, or a welcome or settings check that needs an image already being built waits for that build and shares how it ended, rather than starting another, so two builds never race to tag the same image. A build is tagged only once it has succeeded, so a build that fails or is interrupted never leaves an image that is taken for a good one, and the next need of it builds it again.
A build that fails, or a harness left out of it, is never shown as a wall of Podman's output. The run, the login view, or the welcome check shows a short message in plain words saying what went wrong and what can be done, with a button for each fix the application can make itself, then, collapsed beneath a "Details" disclosure, the step it failed at and everything the build printed, as written, and the same is kept in the debug log. So a package version that doesn't exist reads "OpenCode 2.0.14 isn't available to install" with "Use the latest OpenCode", which builds again with it at its latest; no network reads "Couldn't download what the container needs: check your internet connection" with "Try again"; Podman out of disk space reads so, with "Free up space", which runs `podman system prune` once confirmed; and anything else reads "The container couldn't be set up" with "Try again" and "Copy details". The message is in the theme's warning colour, not its error colour, while a fix is offered.

#### Mounts
29:- "Harness", the open project's harness, named in the row as "Codex" and the like, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, never Claude Code unless that is the project's, and with no project open, the harness a new project starts with, its row saying so, found by running its command with `--version`, required, since Code tasks run it on the host. Missing, its guidance names the command and links to the harness's installation instructions, https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/setup for Claude Code, https://github.com/openai/codex for Codex, and https://opencode.ai/docs/ for OpenCode, with a "Choose another harness" button that opens the Agent section of the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope).
33:- "Harness login", required, named for the same harness as the row above, passing while that harness is logged in in its container, read from its volume. Not logged in, its guidance offers "Log in", which shows the login view, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says. It is checked only once "Containers" passes.
40:"Check again" runs every check anew. The harness checks run anew by themselves whenever another project is opened or the open project's harness is changed, so they never speak of a harness the project doesn't use. A check whose action, as setting up Podman or logging in, finishes runs again by itself, and so do the checks waiting on it. A link opened in the browser leaves the page as it is, until Check again.

Your build failed because the container image pins OpenCode to `opencode-ai@2.0.14`, the version read from your machine, and npm has no such version (its latest is 1.18.35). That one bad version made the single shared install step fail, taking Claude Code and Codex down with it. Each harness now installs on its own, and failures are explained in plain words with buttons to fix them. All tests pass, including new ones, but I haven't run a real image build, login or the Welcome page here.

- **Versions are checked first:** a version read from your machine is used only if `npm view <package>@<version> version` confirms npm has it. Otherwise that harness installs at its latest. Only a plain version number is taken from what your machine's command prints.
- **One harness can't break the others:** each harness gets its own install step, falling back to the latest version and then to leaving it out. A harness left out doesn't fail the build; only runs that need it do.
- **Guidance instead of walls of output:** a failed build now gives a short plain-words message instead of Podman's output:

  | Problem | Message | Buttons |
  |---|---|---|
  | Version not on npm | "OpenCode 2.0.14 isn't available to install" | Use the latest OpenCode |
  | No network | "Couldn't download what the container needs: check your internet connection" | Try again |
  | Podman out of disk space | Says so | Free up space (runs `podman system prune` after you confirm) |
  | Anything else | "The container couldn't be set up" | Try again, Copy details |

  In the login view it's in the warning colour, with Podman's output collapsed under "Details" and also written to the debug log.
- **Welcome:** the harness rows are named for the open project's harness, such as "Codex" and "Codex login". With no project open, the row says it's for new projects. The checks run again when you open another project.
- **Version differences:** if a harness runs a different version in its container than on your machine, Welcome and Settings' Containers section note it in muted text, not as an error.

Places this falls short of the spec:
- **Failed runs:** a run that fails on the build shows the short message as an ordinary error row, offering only the main fix as its button. The Details are in its raw output and the debug log rather than a collapsible section.
- **Changing the harness in Settings:** Welcome re-checks immediately when you open another project. After changing the open project's harness, it re-checks the next time the Welcome page redraws, not instantly.
- **"Use the latest":** this choice lasts only until Suspense restarts. After that, the npm check prevents the bad version from coming back anyway.
